strings.name: Oliver Blume
strings.role: Volkswagen Group CEO and former Porsche AG CEO
strings.summary: Oliver Blume moved from automotive production and planning into group management, leading Porsche and then Volkswagen Group. Porsche went public in 2022 during his tenure. He handed over its CEO role at the end of 2025 while continuing to lead Volkswagen Group. In a 2026 interview, he discussed competitive pressures and restructuring plans.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through 17 November 2026. Porsche and Volkswagen tenures are recorded separately; the term through 2030 is a contractual arrangement, and restructuring plans are not achieved results.
strings.influence.rationale: Held leadership responsibilities at Porsche and Volkswagen Group, participating in vehicle electrification and the transformation of global production.
strings.facts.f1.label: Engineering education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a mechanical engineering degree at TU Braunschweig in 1994 and a doctorate in vehicle engineering at Tongji University in Shanghai in 2001.
strings.facts.f2.label: End of the dual CEO role
strings.facts.f2.value: Michael Leiters became Porsche CEO on 1 January 2026; Blume remained Volkswagen Group CEO.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Porsche IPO
strings.highlights.h1.text: Porsche AG preferred shares began trading in Frankfurt on 29 September 2022, a corporate milestone during his leadership.
strings.highlights.h2.title: From manufacturing to group management
strings.highlights.h2.text: His career spans Audi, SEAT, the Volkswagen brand and Porsche, including production planning and logistics.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Interview on restructuring
strings.timeline.t1.text: An NDR interview published his views on competition and restructuring; the plans still required implementation and necessary approvals.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Dual CEO tenure ends
strings.timeline.t2.text: Michael Leiters took over at Porsche, while Blume continued to lead Volkswagen Group.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Volkswagen renewal announced
strings.timeline.t3.text: The supervisory board agreed to a five-year contract starting in 2026, with a term through the end of 2030.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes Volkswagen Group CEO
strings.timeline.t4.text: Began chairing Volkswagen Group’s Board of Management while still serving as Porsche CEO.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes Porsche CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Matthias Müller; the appointment had been announced the previous day.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Takes charge of Porsche production and logistics
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined Porsche’s Executive Board with responsibility for production and logistics.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Moves to Volkswagen production planning
strings.timeline.t7.text: Took responsibility for production planning at the Volkswagen brand in Wolfsburg.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Starts in Audi’s trainee program
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joined Audi’s international trainee program after completing his mechanical engineering studies.
